title: Literary Theory
tagline: What literature is, literature and society, the creative process, the levels of a literary work, narrative, lyric, drama, genre and style, reading and interpretation, and the schools of modern theory
summary: Literary theory asks what literature is, how it is made, how a work is built and how readers make sense of it. This course introduces those questions through both the Chinese and the Western traditions: literature’s relation to society and to the writer, the levels of a literary work, the theory of narrative, lyric and drama, genre and style, the reader’s part in interpretation, and a map of the main twentieth-century schools from formalism to cultural studies.
overview: An entry course to thinking about literature: what counts as literature, what it does to societies and to readers, and what the work itself is made of.

It moves along three axes—the text (levels, genre, style), the utterance (creation, narrative, lyric, drama) and the reception (interpretation, schools)—so that a reader can locate any critical sentence inside one coherent map.

Chinese and Western materials are braided throughout: from Wenxin Diaolong and the schools of shifen and xiaopin to mimesis, formalism and postcolonialism, ending with an honest inventory of what theory can and cannot do for reading.
outcomes: State and test the classical definitions of literature (mimesis, expression, form, institution) against concrete cases
Explain the major models of the literary circuit—world, work, author, reader—and their signature blind spots
Analyse a narrative by voice, focalisation and time; a lyric by persona and address; a drama by speech-act and staging
Distinguish genre and style claims from value judgments, and use both sets of vocabularies precisely
Summarise the core theses of Russian Formalism, New Criticism, structuralism, psychoanalytic, Marxist, feminist and postcolonial criticism
Evaluate interpretations by their own criteria rather than by taste, and defend a reading with textual evidence
Read classical Chinese criticism (shifen, bixing, xingling, shenyun) as theory, not as impressionism
Position one's own critical instincts within the map and name their assumptions

chapters.title: What literature is
chapters.summary: Definitions of literature in China and the West, literature as an art of language, and the boundaries of the literary.

chapters.title: Literature and society
chapters.summary: Imitation and expression, literature as a reflection of life, ideology, and the market.

chapters.title: The creative process
chapters.summary: Inspiration and craft, experience and imagination, and what writers have said about how they work.

chapters.title: The levels of a literary work
chapters.summary: Language, image and meaning, from Wang Bi’s words, images and ideas to Ingarden’s strata.

chapters.title: Narrative
chapters.summary: Story and discourse, narrators and point of view, and time and plot in narrative works.

chapters.title: Lyric
chapters.summary: The lyric self, image and *yijing*, and the Chinese traditions of poetry as the expression of intent and of feeling.

chapters.title: Drama
chapters.summary: Conflict, character and action, tragedy and comedy, and Chinese opera compared with Western drama.

chapters.title: Genre and style
chapters.summary: Classifying genres, the Chinese theory of genres, and individual and period style.

chapters.title: Reading and interpretation
chapters.summary: The reader’s part, the hermeneutic circle and reception theory, and the Chinese ideas of knowing the author and meeting the author’s intent.

chapters.title: Schools of modern theory
chapters.summary: Formalism, New Criticism, structuralism, psychoanalysis, Marxist criticism, feminism, postcolonialism and cultural studies in outline.

history.title: Plato expels the poets
history.detail: The Republic charges imitative poetry with feeding the passions and removing readers from truth; Western theorising begins as a prosecution.

history.title: Aristotle replies with the Poetics
history.detail: Mimesis is redefined as a universalising, plot-making activity; catharsis gives the defence verdict that launches two millennia of debate.

history.title: Literature as great enterprise
history.detail: Cao Pi's On Literature declares literature the great enterprise of governing the world, an endless undertaking—China's first autonomy claim for letters.

history.title: The literary mind and its articulations
history.detail: Liu Xie's Wenxin Diaolong maps textual styles, genres, creativity and the problem of expression in one systematic work.

history.title: Reflection replaces expression
history.detail: Wordsworth and Coleridge's Lyrical Ballads turns criticism toward the poet's mind and ordinary speech; Romantic expressivism opens the modern era.

history.title: Defamiliarisation
history.detail: Shklovsky makes estrangement the purpose of art; Russian Formalism turns criticism into a science of devices.

history.title: The intentional fallacy
history.detail: Wimsatt and Beardsley, followed by Barthes's death of the author, evict the writer from the courtroom of meaning.

history.title: Orientalism
history.detail: Said shows scholarship as an apparatus of the imperial encounter; postcolonial criticism reframes the canon as world literature in conflict.
